title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a short self-contained lemma characterising the union of all CM fields inside Q̄ ⊂ C. Notation: π1(Q) = Gal(Q̄/Q), τ is ordinary complex conjugation, and Q' is the field of all totally real algebraic numbers (Q^tr).

Preamble. A number field K, given as the fixed field of an open subgroup H ⊂ π1(Q), is totally real exactly when H contains no conjugate of τ. This is the Galois-theoretic way of saying that every embedding of K lands in R.

A) Let L = K(x) be quadratic over K, with x² + ax + b = 0. For the trace and norm Grothendieck writes a = x + x̄ and b = x x̄. Here σ, the generator of Gal(L|K), acts as x ↦ x̄; this holds once L is totally imaginary, which forces complex conjugation to restrict to σ under every embedding. The claim: L is totally imaginary iff the discriminant Δ = a² − 4b = (x − x̄)² is totally strictly negative, i.e. negative under every real embedding of K. In other words, L/K is a CM extension.

B) Let x ∈ Q̄ ⊂ C. Three conditions are equivalent:
- (1) x + x̄ is totally real and (x − x̄)² is totally strictly negative. Then x x̄ is automatically totally real, since x x̄ = ¼[(x + x̄)² − (x − x̄)²].
- (2) There is a totally real K and a totally imaginary quadratic extension L/K (a CM field) with x a generator of L over K.
- (2') x ∈ Q'(i) − Q'.

Proofs:
- (2) ⇒ (1) follows from A).
- (1) ⇒ (2): take K = Q(x + x̄, x x̄) and apply A).

Remark on the page: this shows that condition (1), which depends on the chosen embedding through the bar, is stable under Galois conjugation. That is not evident directly.

C) The same lemma without the word 'generator'. The following are equivalent: (1) as above; (2) x lies in some CM field L; (3) x ∈ Q'(i). Hence Q'(i) = Q^tr(i) is exactly the union Q^cm of all CM fields.

A fourth condition is appended below a line, with a questioning arrow (apparently 3 ⇒ 4 only): (4) x_α x̄_α is totally positive for every conjugate x_α of x. This is the kind of condition met by Weil numbers, where |x_α|² = q.

Purpose. In a dossier on the 'Galois theory of motives' this prepares the description of the field generated by Weil numbers and CM motives. Weil q-numbers lie in Q^cm, so motives over finite fields and CM motives have coefficient or Frobenius fields inside Q'(i). That is the setting of the Serre group and the later Taniyama group.
errors: Sign convention: with x² + ax + b = 0 one has a = −(x + x̄), not a = x + x̄. This is harmless for the discriminant argument.

In A), the statement 'σx = x̄ for all x' presupposes L totally imaginary over totally real K (or at least that complex conjugation does not fix L). It is not a general fact for an arbitrary quadratic L/K.

Condition C4 ⇒ C3 is left with a '?'. The page gives no proof. The easy direction (x ∈ Q^cm ⇒ |σx|² totally positive for all σ) is fine. The converse is not established here: I checked a few small cases (S3 cubic examples, cases forcing totally real x), but I am unsure whether it holds in general.
The crossed-out attempts at the bottom of A) and the struck 3) 'x x̄ est tot. st. positif' show that Grothendieck first had the sign wrong (positive instead of negative) and corrected it.

ideas.what: A totally real field is characterised by its open subgroup H ⊂ Gal(Q̄/Q) containing no conjugate of complex conjugation.
ideas.modern_name: Galois-theoretic characterisation of totally real fields

ideas.what: A quadratic extension L/K of a totally real field is totally imaginary iff its discriminant is totally negative; then complex conjugation induces the same automorphism under every embedding.

The union of all CM fields equals Q^tr(i), with elementwise criteria: x + x̄ totally real and (x − x̄)² totally negative. These conditions are Galois-stable even though they are phrased via a fixed embedding.
ideas.modern_name: Q^cm = Q^tr(i), the maximal CM subfield of Q̄
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard; used by Serre (Serre group), Deligne, Langlands, Milne

ideas.what: Proposed (with '?') characterisation of Q^cm by |x_α|² being totally positive for every conjugate x_α, generalising the fact that Weil numbers generate CM or totally real fields.
ideas.modern_name: Weil numbers lie in Q^cm; characterisations of CM fields via absolute values of conjugates
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil-number fact standard (Honda–Tate era); field characterisations in later notes, e.g. Blanksby–Loxton (unsure of exact content)

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks whether Q^cm can be characterised purely by the norms x_α x̄_α of all conjugates being totally positive. He leaves it with a question mark. This would be a slightly stronger statement than the standard 'Weil numbers lie in a CM field'.
missed.quote: 4) x x̄ tot positif, ... x_α x̄_α pour tt conjugué x_α de x
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a small, elementary question about CM fields. It is of minor interest unless it turns out false in an instructive way; specialists likely know the answer or an equivalent statement.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a clean but standard lemma: CM fields and Q^cm = Q^tr(i), the kind of preliminary needed for Weil numbers and CM motives. Its only non-routine element is a questioned extra criterion. It mainly documents that Grothendieck worked with Q^cm in the motivic-Galois context, which is expected rather than surprising.
transcription_corrections: Line 'En effet, 2)⇒1) ne résulte de A)' should read roughly 'En effet, 2)⇒1) résulte de A)'; 'ne' is a misreading.
In C) 4), 'pour H conjugué x_α de x' should be 'pour tt conjugué x_α de x'. Above it is a struck word ('épais'?), and 'défini par' is probably 'ainsi que' / 'de même pour'.
In C) 2), 'x ∈ [-K-] L': the K is struck and replaced by L (x ∈ L).
The arrow before C) 4) is '?⇑' in the margin, indicating that only one direction is asserted and the equivalence is doubted.
In B), 'Remarque Cet [?]' is likely 'Cet argument' or 'Ce qui précède prouve...'.
